text: I’m a Computer Science graduate from Penn State with a strong foundation in backend systems, embedded software, and full-stack development. As a full-stack developer, I’ve built data-driven web platforms using the MERN stack and MySQL, including a B2B eCommerce system and dynamic support ticketing workflows. My AI projects include integrating the OpenAI API into real-world applications with semantic search and typewriter-style response rendering. I’ve also engineered a peer-to-peer file sharing network, an AR iOS furniture layout app with RealityKit, and a custom memory allocator in C. I’m passionate about building scalable, user-centric systems—from embedded tools to end-to-end platforms—and excited to contribute to engineering teams solving real-world problems.

title: AI Portfolio Website
text: AI Portfolio Website – An AI-powered personal portfolio website featuring an interactive ChatGPT stlye chatbot that answers recruiter questions using a custom RAG pipeline and OpenAI's GPT-4o.

title: AI Portfolio Website
text: I engineered a full-stack AI portfolio website that integrates a ChatGPT-style assistant capable of answering dynamic questions about my background, experience, and projects. Built with a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, the chatbot uses OpenAI’s `text-embedding-ada-002` model for semantic search over embedded content chunks and GPT-4o for natural language generation. I implemented cosine similarity logic, fine-tuned scoring heuristics, and a dual-layer chunking system for context resolution. On the frontend, I recreated the ChatGPT UI using React and CSS Modules, with features like dynamic message typing, mobile responsiveness, animated modals, and form-to-email integration via Formspree. I handled rate limiting, edge case fallbacks, and OpenAI error scenarios with user-friendly responses. The site includes full SEO metadata, Open Graph image support, and deployment to Vercel using environment variables and statically served assets for optimal performance. Tech stack: Next.js, React, OpenAI API, Node.js Period: Summer 2025 Type: Personal Project

title: Peer-to-Peer File Sharing System
text: Peer-to-Peer File Sharing System – A Python-based P2P file-sharing network with chunked transfers, multi-threaded downloads, and built-in integrity checks for fast and reliable file distribution.

title: Peer-to-Peer File Sharing System
text: I designed a peer-to-peer (P2P) file-sharing network in Python, featuring a central server and multiple peers to enable efficient and decentralized file distribution. The system uses a chunk-based approach to split large files, allowing simultaneous downloads from multiple peers, which significantly improves overall download speed. I implemented multi-threading to handle parallel connections smoothly and ensure scalability. To maintain data integrity, I integrated hashing-based checks that verify the accuracy of downloaded chunks and discard any corrupted data. Tech stack: Python Period: Fall 2024 Type: Academic Project

title: Causal Consistency Simulation
text: Causal Consistency Simulation – A Python-based distributed system that simulates causal consistency across multiple data centers using Lamport clocks and dependency tracking.

title: Causal Consistency Simulation
text: I developed a distributed system simulation to demonstrate causal consistency using three interlinked data centers. Each datacenter tracks dependencies between write operations using Lamport clocks to maintain causality and ensure that messages are delivered in a consistent order. I implemented FIFO message delivery and Lamport timestamping to enforce correct inter-datacenter communication. The system models realistic delay patterns and highlights how causally-related writes are respected across the network even when operating asynchronously. This helped me deepen my understanding of consistency models and their tradeoffs in distributed architectures. Tech stack: Python Period: Fall 2024 Type: Academic Project

title: Dynamic Storage Allocator
text: Dynamic Storage Allocator – A custom C dynamic memory allocator featuring optimized malloc/realloc/free, segregated free lists, and a heap consistency checker for robust memory management.

title: Dynamic Storage Allocator
text: I developed a dynamic memory allocator for C programs by implementing custom versions of malloc, realloc, and free, with a focus on optimizing space utilization and throughput. This was achieved through techniques such as block header/footer optimization, coalescing of free blocks, and the use of size-based segregated linked lists for efficient allocation. To ensure reliable memory management, I also created a heap consistency checker that runs in debugging mode to detect and resolve heap inconsistencies. Tech stack: C Period: Spring 2024 Type: Academic Project

title: Linear Device Library
text: Linear Device Library – A C-based Linux utility that combines 16 JBODs into a 1 MB linear device with read/write support, LRU caching, and TCP networking for efficient storage access.

title: Linear Device Library
text: I designed and developed a Linux mdadm-style utility in C to configure 16 JBOD devices, each 64 KB in size, into a single coherent 1 MB linear storage device. I implemented core read and write functionalities that allowed access to the storage architecture using a user-provided buffer. To enhance performance and flexibility, I introduced an LRU caching mechanism that reduced the cost of JBOD operations by 30%, and added networking support by developing a client component to communicate with the embedded JBOD server over TCP. Tech stack: C, Linux Period: Spring 2023 Type: Academic Project

title: Mini CPU
text: Mini CPU – A Verilog-based 5-stage MIPS pipeline with ALU-to-ALU data forwarding and hazard resolution for optimized execution of R-type instructions.

title: Mini CPU
text: I designed and developed a comprehensive 5-stage MIPS pipeline in Verilog to execute R-type arithmetic instructions efficiently. To optimize CPU performance and ensure accurate data processing, I implemented data-forwarding modules using a state machine, enabling ALU-to-ALU forwarding and effective handling of data hazards. This included integrating detailed case handling to support accurate and reliable data manipulation across pipeline stages. Tech stack: Verilog Period: Fall 2023 Type: Academic Project

text: Course Scheduler App – A database-driven course scheduler with role-based access, built using OOP principles, SQL, and a tabbed GUI for organized course and student management.

title: Furniture Store App
text: Furniture Store App – An iOS AR app for virtual room decor that lets users place, scale, and move life-size furniture models in real-world spaces with saved layouts and guided setup.

title: Furniture Store App
text: I created an immersive iOS virtual room decor app designed to help users plan furniture placement in their actual living spaces, eliminating the need to visit multiple furniture stores. The app features a picture menu at the bottom of the interface, allowing users to select and place life-sized furniture models in the real world with a tap. I enhanced these models with functionality for scaling, rotation, and movement to provide a realistic and flexible design experience. To support new users, I integrated an AR Coaching Overlay that guides them through app setup and room scanning. The app also includes persistence to save virtual room maps, displays real-time mapping status for debugging, and offers a clear button to delete saved maps along with an undo button to remove the last added model. Tech stack: ARKit, RealityKit, Swift Period: Summer 2022 Type: Personal Project

title: Measurement App
text: Measurement App – An iOS AR measurement app that lets users mark two points in the real world to calculate distances, with logging, undo, and guided setup features.

title: Measurement App
text: I created an iOS virtual measurement app that allows users to measure the distance between two real-world points using augmented reality, supported by an AR Coaching Overlay for guided setup. Users can place two model entities with a tap to mark the points, and the app calculates and displays the distance in meters. I implemented a logging feature to store all measurement records, along with a clear button to reset the log and an undo button to remove the last entry, enhancing the overall user experience. Tech stack: ARKit, RealityKit, Swift Period: Summer 2022 Type: Personal Project
